# Introduction

We describe BMI–hypercapnia relationships within a selected acute-care cohort while exposing how historical source-entry pathways shape the observed population. These pathways record representation in reason-for-suspicion (RFS) source files; they do not necessarily identify every clinical criterion present at an encounter. Separating entry routes can change the observed association itself and does not eliminate outcome-dependent selection.

# Methods

## Source, eligibility and fixed index

The authenticated original FULL_DATA encounter list defines candidate visits. Adults had a 2022 emergency or inpatient encounter and any available valid BMI, without an obesity restriction. Age uses the inherited birth-year proxy. Each patient contributes the first qualifying encounter before gas availability and adjustment completeness. Earlier unresolved eligibility, conflicting evidence and earliest-date ties remain unresolved. Later encounters never replace an obesity-only index.

BMI follows the approved encounter/prior reported-value hierarchy, followed by calculation from observed height and weight, with inherited rounding and validity rules. One-unit diagnostic bins around BMI 40 and 50 describe measurement and selection; they are not a regression-discontinuity design. No statistical BMI imputation is performed. Available BMI is not necessarily contemporaneous with the outcome. The audit reports measurement methods, lags, unknown chronology and consequences of the existing rules. Signed lags equal encounter-start date minus measurement date: positive means prior, zero means the same calendar day, and negative means later during the encounter. Component gaps are absolute differences between height and weight dates.


### Usable gas evidence and ascertainment

A usable result is at least one captured ordinary, unadjusted PCO₂ measurement linked to the selected encounter, with authenticated arterial or venous specimen assignment, reviewed units convertible to mm Hg, and strict validity limits of 5 < arterial PCO₂ <200 or 10 < venous PCO₂ <250 mm Hg. Normal and elevated results both establish usable evidence; neither hypercapnia nor pH is required. Temperature-adjusted, nonnumeric, specimen-ambiguous/conflicting, unsupported-unit and out-of-range measurements do not establish usable evidence.

Ascertainment is encounter-wide, including results recorded later in the stay or after treatment. It is not restricted to the encounter-start day or a pretreatment draw. Separate ABG and VBG observation models use the primary fixed BMI spline and the shared setting-inclusive adjustment, standardized over all adjustment-complete primary patients. The endpoints indicate usable captured evidence, not every test ordered or drawn. No usable result does not establish no testing or physiological normality. Patients can have both specimens, so these probabilities are not mutually exclusive. In F1-main, panel C's gray band describes the joint total; component intervals appear in the landmark table.

## Historical source-entry populations

A confirmed positive ABG, VBG, RESPFAIL, VENTSUPPORT or PREDISPOSITION source flag establishes the primary population, including encounters also represented through OBESITY. Obesity-only membership requires OBESITY and authenticated zeros in all five other families. Obesity-only indexes are excluded from scientific comparisons: removing the gas-related entry pathways selects against the evidence needed to assess the physiological outcomes. Their counts remain in the detailed audit flow for reconciliation; source discrepancies and descriptive profiles are confined to the audit. Unknown flags remain unknown. All-six-zero discrepancies require source investigation. RFS metadata are applied after the common index is selected.

The combined indexed cohort is a reconciliation reference. Non-OBESITY-only, overlapping and unknown-OBESITY/confirmed-non-OBESITY subgroups are descriptive. BMI ≥40 remains a descriptive stratum and is not equated with obesity-route membership. The nested BMI ≥30 secondary analysis retains the newly selected primary index and never promotes a later obese encounter. All three endpoint families are refitted within this secondary population. The overlapping all-OBESITY-route analysis and current-measurement analysis remain supporting checks.

## Outcomes and adjustment

Arterial hypercapnia requires ordinary authenticated ABG PaCO~2~ ≥45 mm Hg. Combined gas accepts ABG PaCO~2~ ≥45 or VBG PvCO~2~ ≥50 mm Hg; both specimens are not required. No pH restriction is applied to the established primary outcomes. Strict validity limits are 5<arterial<200 and 10<venous<250 mm Hg, with reviewed units. Available-evidence negatives do not establish that an unmeasured specimen is normal. Unusable or unavailable outcomes remain unknown.

The ICD composite comprises J96.02, J96.12, J96.22, J96.92 and E66.2, with captured absence negative only under complete diagnosis capture. E66.2 introduces obesity-related ascertainment. Index-calendar-day gas sensitivities use recorded-result date equal to encounter-start date, retaining the index. This export does not authenticate collection times.

Adjustment includes linear age, inherited sex, combined race/ethnicity and geographic-region coding, and index encounter setting (EMER emergency as reference; IMP inpatient) as a categorical main effect in every fitted model. No BMI-by-setting interaction is fitted. Standardization retains each patient's observed setting. Completeness means nonmissing values for inherited analysis variables, including retained Unknown categories. The White reference category includes non-Hispanic or unknown ethnicity; inherited race-category precedence is unchanged. Raw race × ethnicity cross-tabs are shown only when authenticated.

## Models, probabilities and uncertainty

Each main population uses type-7 BMI quantiles .05/.35/.65/.95 from its own adjustment-complete population: two interior knots, two boundaries and three natural-spline basis columns. The basis remains fixed across its binary and joint endpoint families and predictions; primary timing and matched checks retain the primary basis. The primary current-measurement sensitivity reuses this basis. The overlapping all-OBESITY supporting analysis uses its own basis and is reported in the audit. Obesity-only and obesity-only current-measurement models are not registered. Constant outcomes, duplicate knots, separation, rank and convergence failures in planned models remain explicit without estimator substitution.

Gas curves standardize over each model's outcome-evaluable population; ICD uses known capture within group. Observation curves describe usable gas-evidence availability. Complete diagnosis capture is reported as a source fact, not as ICD positivity or a constant availability curve. No physiological outcomes are projected to untested patients. Contrasts over supported five-unit intervals are audit summaries, including 40 versus 45; the full supported BMI range organizes the presentation. Local counts and marginal covariate coverage expose sparsity even inside the global BMI range; these checks do not establish joint covariate support.

Pointwise 95% intervals use full coefficient covariance and condition on the empirical reference and fixed spline basis. They omit uncertainty from selection, measurement error and unmeasured confounding. Apparent calibration is in-sample; fitted/observed mean agreement is not independent validation.

## Secondary scenario and supporting checks

The named secondary scenario subtracts exactly one BMI unit when observed BMI >30; BMI≤30 is unchanged. There is no floor or reselection. Paired predictions hold index, RFS membership and other covariates fixed. Reported quantities are observed and shifted mean probabilities, their signed difference and PIF=1−p_shifted/p_observed. Patients with BMI ≤30 remain in the entire model reference denominator and baseline modeled burden; their scenario difference is exactly zero. Signed original-BMI-band contributions and their full covariance reproduce the total difference and variance. Marginal curve-density integration is not used.

Same-sample linear-BMI checks and matched ICD/gas analyses remain registered. A limited current-measurement sensitivity uses the already-selected BMI when reported at the index or calculated from height and weight both authenticated to that encounter. Full-cohort MAR/MNAR projections and IPW are excluded. The report is rendered from saved aggregates without clinical reads or refitting.

## Same-day physiological components

The physiological component analysis uses any recorded calendar date within the existing index encounter with both usable ordinary arterial PCO~2~ and arterial pH. It is **same recorded-day co-occurrence; not verified same-sample pairing**. The export dates when results were recorded; it does not identify a shared blood sample, collection time or elapsed 24-hour interval. Validity screens are 5<PCO~2~<200 mm Hg and 6.5<pH<7.8, applied before display rounding.

The source endpoints use the same patients with at least one co-observed day: any PaCO~2~ ≥45 on such a day, and any such day also containing pH <7.35. Results may come from different samples. Elevated PCO~2~ on one date and low pH on another cannot establish co-occurrence. Patients without a valid co-observed day have unknown component outcomes. Additional unusable or single-analyte records remain audited without erasing usable days. A negative describes eligible recorded evidence only. The relevant population’s numeric BMI spline basis, specified adjustment and common component reference population are retained. A single unpenalized multinomial logistic spline assigns each patient to no documented hypercapnia, hypercapnia without documented same-day acidemia, or hypercapnia with same-day acidemia. Any eligible hypercapnia–acidemia day takes priority, including patients with other hypercapnic days without acidemia. The baseline outcome is no documented hypercapnia. All three probabilities are standardized over the same patients; full cross-category covariance supplies pointwise intervals and comparisons of component changes. No additional PIF is calculated.

The full observed BMI range is the main relationship, with sparse regions flagged. BMI 40–45 is a prespecified numerical summary, not a biological cutoff or fitting restriction. Every supported five-unit interval is also reported. These are descriptive pointwise contrasts without multiplicity adjustment; separate significance counts do not establish differences in associations.

## Diagnostic components

The diagnostic component analysis partitions the inherited five-code ICD composite on the same fixed indexes within each main population. It requires complete encounter diagnosis capture and nonmissing specified adjustment variables, including retained Unknown categories; it does not require blood gas evidence. J96.22 or J96.02 together with J96.12/E66.2 receives priority as **acute-on-chronic or concurrent acute/chronic coding**. Remaining J96.02 is acute; remaining J96.12/E66.2 is chronic coding/OHS; remaining J96.92 is unspecified acuity. No target code with complete capture is the reference category. Incomplete capture is unknown. OHS is grouped analytically with chronic coding and does not itself establish chronic respiratory failure.

One Firth mean-bias-reduced five-category multinomial spline reuses its population’s numeric BMI basis, linear age, inherited sex, race/ethnicity and region, and categorical encounter-setting adjustment. All class probabilities are standardized over the same diagnosis-evaluable patients. The estimator maximizes the multinomial log likelihood plus one half of the log determinant of its Fisher information. It replaces a separated unpenalized fit without pooling demographic levels or changing categories. The inverse multinomial information at the bias-reduced estimate supplies first-order joint covariance, with the empirical reference and numeric spline held fixed. This finite-estimate method does not resolve sparse support, source selection or measurement bias. Full joint covariance supplies pointwise 95% intervals, supported five-unit changes and pairwise differences in those changes. These descriptive comparisons are not multiplicity adjusted. The fitted positive components sum to the joint composite; it need not equal the existing binary model's predictions. No component-specific PIF is calculated.

The unpenalized four-category sensitivity excludes only the final unspecified-only category. Mixed codes assigned to specified categories remain included. It retains its population’s fixed basis and adjustment but uses its own reduced fitting/reference population. This is not a same-denominator estimator comparison. Failed positions remain explicit.

# Results

## Cohort construction and evidence availability

figure("F0-primary-gas");figure("RFS-evidence")
bmi_report_table(a$rfs_summary,"Fixed-index RFS partition",keys="population_id")
setting<-a$category_counts[a$category_counts$population_id=="primary::C" & a$category_counts$variable_id=="encounter_type",]
bmi_report_table(setting,"Encounter setting in the primary reference",keys="level")
nested<-a$cohort_nodes[a$cohort_nodes$population_id %in% c("primary::Q","primary_bmi_ge30::Q"),]
bmi_report_table(nested,"Nested secondary membership at the same index",keys="population_id")
capture<-bmi_rfs_availability(a);capture<-capture[capture$population_id=="primary" & capture$outcome_id=="icd",]
cat("Known diagnosis capture: ",format(capture$M,big.mark=",")," / ",format(capture$N,big.mark=","),
    " primary indexes. Capture is not ICD positivity. All patient/outcome counts below use the common cohort ledger.\n\n",sep="")
```

 bmi_grouped_report(profile,"Participant profiles",groups="variable_id")

 bmi_report_table(v$model_registry[v$model_registry$model_id %in% primary,],"Binary model status",keys="model_id")
 cat("\n### Same-day physiological components\n\n")

 z<-v$cooccurrence_reconciliation
 shown<-data.frame(Stage=z$stage,Patients=z$n,Events=z$events,
  Observed=ifelse(is.na(z$proportion),"Unavailable",bmi_percent_ci(100*z$proportion,100*z$conf_low,100*z$conf_high)),Status=z$status)
 bmi_report_table(shown,"Patient selection, day restriction and acidemia; Wilson 95% intervals",keys="Stage")
 figure(paste0(group,"/S1-same-day-ABG"))
 bmi_report_table(v$cooccurrence_categories,"Mutually exclusive same-day components",keys="category_id")
 cat("Same recorded-day co-occurrence; not verified same-sample pairing. Different samples and treatment periods may contribute. Requiring co-observation changes the available-evidence population; no inference about compensation or acute respiratory failure follows.\n\n")
 cat("\n### Diagnostic components\n\n")
 bmi_report_table(v$icd_acuity_status,"Code-level diagnosis source status",keys="module")
 fit<-v$model_registry[v$model_registry$family %in% c("same_day_abg","icd_acuity","icd_acuity_specified"),]
 fit$estimator[fit$family=="same_day_abg"]<-"Unpenalized multinomial logit"
 bmi_report_table(fit[c("model_id","estimator","n_model","status","failure_reason")],"Joint model estimability",keys="model_id")
 z<-v$icd_acuity_categories
 shown<-data.frame(Category=z$label,Patients=z$n,N=z$N,
  Observed=ifelse(is.na(z$proportion),"Unavailable",bmi_percent_ci(100*z$proportion,100*z$conf_low,100*z$conf_high)),Status=z$status)
 bmi_report_table(shown,"Observed diagnostic components; Wilson 95% intervals",keys="Category")
 for(id in c("S2-ICD-acuity","S2-ICD-specified","S2-ICD-observed"))figure(paste0(group,"/",id))
 cat("Diagnostic codes describe documentation, not acidemia or compensation. OHS is grouped analytically with chronic coding; diagnostic incorporation and source entry can affect its BMI association. Complete component contrast tables and their joint covariance are retained in the audit.\n\n")
 cat("\n### Modeled burden under the one-unit BMI scenario\n\n")
 bmi_report_table(bmi_pif_view(v,primary),"Paired model-standardized scenario",keys="Model")
 figure(paste0(group,"/F2"))
 cat("Baseline burden includes all reference patients, including those at BMI ≤30 who have zero scenario difference. PIF is relative to that entire modeled baseline burden. These conditional model changes are not estimates of preventable cases or treatment efficacy.\n\n")
 bmi_report_table(v$model_fit_diagnostics[v$model_fit_diagnostics$model_id %in% primary,],"Binary apparent fit diagnostics",keys="metric")
 bmi_report_table(v$prediction_support,"Curve and transformed prediction support",keys="model_id")
}
```

## Other sensitivities and verification

```{r}
#| results: asis
v<-bmi_group_view(a,"primary")
bmi_report_table(v$timing_audit,"Fixed-index calendar-day transitions",keys="outcome_id")
bmi_report_table(v$linear_spline_comparison,"Same-sample linear checks",keys="outcome_id")
for(o in c("abg","any_gas")){figure(paste0("primary/F5-timing-",o));figure(paste0("primary/F5-matched-",o))}
bmi_report_table(a$bmi_provenance[a$bmi_provenance$stage=="Q" & a$bmi_provenance$subgroup %in% c("non_obesity_only","overlap","non_obesity_with_unknown_obesity"),],"Primary BMI provenance and lags",keys="subgroup")
for(group in c("primary_current","all_obesity")) {
 v<-bmi_group_view(a,group)
 cat("\n### ",bmi_analysis_label(group),"\n\n",sep="")
 bmi_report_table(v$model_registry,"Supporting fit status",keys="model_id")
 bmi_report_table(bmi_pif_view(v,primary),"Supporting scenario estimates",keys="Model")
 figure(paste0(group,"/F1-B"))
}
```

The current-measurement restriction retains the same index and primary spline basis. All-OBESITY-route patients overlap the primary cohort; this analysis is not a partition or an independent comparison group. Obesity-only and unresolved source entry remain audit-only. No between-group test follows from separate intervals.

# Interpretation

The primary relationship concerns all valid-BMI patients whose first qualifying encounter was represented through a non-OBESITY source pathway. The nested BMI ≥30 analysis addresses restriction at that same encounter. Broader BMI eligibility can change historical indexes and source-entry classifications; the new cohort is not merely the old cohort plus thinner patients.

The scenario changes exposure only above BMI 30 while retaining unshifted baseline burden below it. Gas findings remain conditional on evaluable evidence. Source entry, selective measurement, BMI timing, diagnostic incorporation, sparse support and residual confounding limit both observed relationships and model-based scenarios. Numerical reconciliation does not confer causal interpretation or investigator approval.

All applicable variables, coefficients, reference levels, covariance matrices, diagnostics, failures and supported contrasts—including 40 versus 45—are provided in the companion audit and aggregate tables. The plots describe relationships across BMI rather than privileging that interval.
